mcqs.stem: Best guess: a small company collected $500,000 from customers this year. Receivables rose from $40,000 to $70,000. What was accrual-basis revenue?

choices.explanation: Rising receivables mean revenue exceeded collections, not the reverse.
That is cash-basis revenue.
This adds the whole ending balance without subtracting the beginning balance.

mcqs.explanation: Accrual revenue = cash collected + ending AR − beginning AR = 500,000 + 70,000 − 40,000 = **530,000**.

mcqs.stem: Which title is appropriate for a cash-basis operating statement?

choices.explanation: That title implies accrual GAAP.

choices.text: Statement of revenues collected and expenses paid
choices.explanation: Correct. The title signals the cash basis.
A GAAP title that would mislead users.
The statements are not GAAP.

mcqs.explanation: Special-purpose statements use titles that avoid implying GAAP; cash-basis operating statements are typically titled 'statement of revenues collected and expenses paid.'

mcqs.stem: A company preparing income-tax-basis statements wrote off $12,000 of uncollectible accounts this year and estimates another $8,000 of current receivables will be uncollectible. What bad debt expense is reported?

choices.explanation: Correct. The tax basis uses the direct write-off method.
This adds an allowance-based estimate, which the tax basis does not use.
The estimate is not deductible until written off.
Actual write-offs are deductible.

mcqs.explanation: Under the income tax basis, bad debts are deducted when specific accounts are written off (direct write-off method). The $8,000 estimate is not recorded.

mcqs.stem: Which of the following is **not** a special purpose framework?

choices.explanation: A special purpose framework.
A special purpose framework.

choices.text: U.S. GAAP for private companies with PCC alternatives
choices.explanation: Correct. PCC alternatives are part of U.S. GAAP, a general purpose framework.

choices.text: A regulatory basis required by a state insurance commission
choices.explanation: A special purpose framework.

mcqs.explanation: Special purpose frameworks include cash, modified cash, tax, regulatory, contractual, and other bases. Private-company GAAP alternatives are still GAAP.

mcqs.stem: Cash paid for rent was $36,000. Prepaid rent was $6,000 at the beginning of the year and $9,000 at the end. What is accrual-basis rent expense?

choices.explanation: This adds the increase in prepaid rent; an increase means cash was paid ahead, so expense is lower.
That is cash-basis expense.
This subtracts the ending balance without adding the beginning.

mcqs.explanation: Expense = cash paid + beginning prepaid (used this year) − ending prepaid (for next year) = 36,000 + 6,000 − 9,000 = **33,000**.

mcqs.stem: A physician's cash receipts from patients were $620,000. Accounts receivable were $70,000 at the beginning and $55,000 at the end of the year; $4,000 of receivables were written off during the year. What is accrual-basis revenue (gross, before any allowance)?

choices.explanation: This subtracts the write-offs, but written-off amounts were billed revenue.
This ignores the write-offs, which reduced receivables without cash.
This reverses the receivable change.

mcqs.explanation: Receivable roll-forward: beginning 70,000 + revenue − collections 620,000 − write-offs 4,000 = ending 55,000 → revenue = 55,000 + 620,000 + 4,000 − 70,000 = **609,000**.

mcqs.stem: Which modification to the cash basis is generally considered to have substantial support under a modified cash basis?

choices.text: Recording revenue when services are performed
choices.explanation: Recognizing receivables broadly converts the statements to accrual, beyond a modification.

choices.text: Deferring rent expense arbitrarily to smooth income
choices.explanation: Arbitrary deferrals have no support.
Estimated accruals are accrual-basis features, not typical modifications.

choices.text: Capitalizing equipment purchases and recording depreciation
choices.explanation: Correct. A common, well-supported modification.

mcqs.explanation: Modifications with substantial support include capitalizing and depreciating long-lived assets, recording long-term debt, and accruing income taxes. Pervasive accruals would make it an accrual basis.

mcqs.stem: In income-tax-basis financial statements, how is interest income on municipal bonds (exempt from federal tax) presented?

choices.text: Excluded entirely because it is not taxable
choices.explanation: Tax-basis statements present all revenues; nontaxable items are still reported.

choices.text: Included as revenue, often shown or disclosed as nontaxable
choices.explanation: Correct. Tax-basis statements include nontaxable revenues and nondeductible expenses, typically as separate line items or with disclosure, so the statements remain complete.
It is revenue of the period.
It belongs in the statement of revenues and expenses.

mcqs.explanation: Tax-basis statements include nontaxable revenues and nondeductible expenses, typically as separate line items or with disclosure, so the statements remain complete.

mcqs.stem: Which disclosure is required in financial statements prepared using a special purpose framework?

choices.text: A reconciliation quantifying every difference from GAAP net income
choices.explanation: Differences must be described, but their effects need not be quantified.

choices.text: A statement that the statements comply with GAAP
choices.explanation: They do not comply with GAAP.

choices.text: A description of the basis of accounting and how it differs from GAAP
choices.explanation: Correct. Special-purpose statements describe the basis and the primary differences from GAAP (without quantifying), and include informative disclosures similar to GAAP where applicable.
Disclosures comparable to GAAP for similar items are expected.

mcqs.explanation: Special-purpose statements describe the basis and the primary differences from GAAP (without quantifying), and include informative disclosures similar to GAAP where applicable.

mcqs.stem: Cash paid for utilities was $24,000. Utilities payable was $3,000 at the beginning of the year and $1,000 at the end. What is accrual utilities expense?

choices.explanation: This reverses the effect of the decrease in payables.
That is the cash amount.
This adds only the ending payable.

mcqs.explanation: Some of the 24,000 paid settled last year's 3,000 bill. Expense = 24,000 + ending payable 1,000 − beginning payable 3,000 = **22,000**.

mcqs.stem: Which title is appropriate for the balance sheet of an entity reporting on the income tax basis?

choices.explanation: 'Balance sheet' implies GAAP; tax-basis titles must signal the basis.
Also a GAAP-style title without a basis qualifier.

choices.text: Statement of assets and liabilities arising from cash transactions
choices.explanation: That is a cash-basis title.

choices.text: Statement of assets, liabilities, and equity — income tax basis
choices.explanation: Correct. Titles should reflect the special purpose framework: 'Statement of assets, liabilities, and equity — income tax basis.'

mcqs.explanation: Titles should reflect the special purpose framework: 'Statement of assets, liabilities, and equity — income tax basis.'

mcqs.stem: A cash-basis entity received $48,000 in advance for a 12-month service contract on October 1. What revenue would be recognized for the calendar year under the accrual basis versus the cash basis?

choices.explanation: Correct. Accrual: 48,000 × 3/12 = 12,000 earned; cash basis records the full receipt.
Reversed — the cash basis records what was received.
The cash basis recognizes all cash received.
Accrual recognizes only the 3 months earned.

mcqs.explanation: Accrual: revenue earned Oct–Dec = 48,000 × 3/12 = **12,000**, with 36,000 unearned. Cash basis: all **48,000** received is revenue.

mcqs.stem: Why might a closely held company choose income-tax-basis statements instead of GAAP?

choices.text: Tax-basis statements are required for all private companies
choices.explanation: No such requirement exists.

choices.text: Tax-basis statements eliminate the need for any disclosures
choices.explanation: Disclosures are still required.

choices.text: Its users accept the tax basis, which is cheaper and ties to the return
choices.explanation: Correct. Special purpose frameworks are appropriate when users agree to them.

choices.text: Tax-basis statements always report higher net income
choices.explanation: Tax basis may report higher or lower income depending on differences.

mcqs.explanation: Special purpose frameworks are appropriate when users agree to them. The tax basis leverages records the company already keeps, reducing cost.

mcqs.stem: A business on the cash basis collected $500,000 from customers. Accounts receivable rose from $40,000 to $55,000, and unearned revenue fell from $10,000 to $6,000. What is accrual-basis revenue?

choices.explanation: Correct. 500,000 + 15,000 AR increase + 4,000 unearned revenue decrease.
The decrease in unearned revenue also adds to revenue.
The increase in receivables adds to revenue.
Both adjustments increase revenue.

mcqs.explanation: Accrual revenue = cash collected + increase in receivables + decrease in unearned revenue.

mcqs.stem: A company paid $300,000 of salaries in cash. Accrued salaries were $12,000 at the beginning of the year and $8,000 at the end. What is accrual-basis salaries expense?

choices.explanation: A decrease in accrued salaries reduces expense.
Cash paid must be adjusted for the accrual change.
Accruals are netted, not added.

mcqs.explanation: Accrual expense = cash paid − beginning accrued liability + ending accrued liability.

mcqs.stem: In financial statements prepared on the pure cash basis, depreciation on equipment is:

choices.explanation: Depreciation is a modification of the cash basis, not pure cash basis.
That would be the income tax basis.
Correct. The pure cash basis records only cash receipts and disbursements; the equipment cost was a disbursement.

choices.text: Recorded only for assets bought on credit
choices.explanation: Pure cash basis ignores noncash expenses.

mcqs.explanation: Under the pure cash basis, the purchase is a cash disbursement; depreciation appears only if the cash basis is modified.

mcqs.stem: A company paid $24,000 of insurance premiums. Prepaid insurance was $6,000 at the beginning of the year and $9,000 at the end. What is accrual-basis insurance expense?

choices.explanation: An increase in prepaid insurance reduces expense.
Cash paid must be adjusted for prepaid changes.
Only the change (3,000) adjusts cash paid.

mcqs.explanation: Accrual expense = cash paid + beginning prepaid − ending prepaid.

mcqs.stem: Statements prepared under a special purpose framework contain items that are the same as, or similar to, items in GAAP statements. What disclosures are required?

choices.explanation: Correct. Informative disclosures similar to GAAP are needed for similar items.

choices.text: No disclosures beyond the basis of accounting
choices.explanation: Similar items require similar disclosures.

choices.text: All disclosures GAAP requires, without exception
choices.explanation: The requirement is for similar informative disclosures.

choices.text: Only disclosures required by the tax law
choices.explanation: The framework still needs informative disclosures.

mcqs.explanation: Under special purpose frameworks, statements include a description of the basis and informative disclosures similar to GAAP for similar items.

mcqs.stem: In income-tax-basis statements, how is depreciation usually computed?

choices.explanation: Tax basis uses tax rules.
Correct. The statements follow tax rules.
Depreciation is recorded.
Fair value isn't the basis.

mcqs.explanation: Income-tax-basis statements measure items using the methods used for the tax return.

mcqs.stem: Under the pure cash basis, how is interest accrued but unpaid on a loan treated at year-end?

choices.explanation: Accruals aren't recorded.
Only paid interest.
Correct. Only cash payments are recorded.

choices.text: In the notes as a liability
choices.explanation: Unpaid interest isn't recorded.

mcqs.explanation: The cash basis records transactions only when cash is received or paid.

mcqs.stem: An insurer prepares statements for its state insurance department under statutory accounting. Which framework is this?

choices.explanation: Statutory accounting differs.
Not the framework.
Not the framework.
Correct. It's a special purpose framework.

mcqs.explanation: Statutory accounting prescribed by a regulator is a regulatory-basis special purpose framework.

mcqs.stem: Accrual revenue is $400,000. Accounts receivable rose $30,000, and unearned revenue rose $10,000. What were cash receipts from customers?

choices.explanation: A receivable increase reduces cash.
Unearned revenue adds cash.
Adjust for both changes.

mcqs.explanation: Cash receipts = revenue − increase in receivables + increase in unearned revenue.

mcqs.stem: Cash paid for supplies was $50,000. Supplies on hand rose $4,000, and accounts payable for supplies fell $2,000. What is accrual supplies expense?

choices.explanation: A payables decrease lowers expense.
Correct. 50 − 4 − 2.
Subtract both changes.
Both changes lower expense.

mcqs.explanation: Expense = cash paid − increase in supplies − decrease in payables.

mcqs.stem: Under the cash basis, $400,000 was collected from customers, and AR rose by $30,000. What is accrual-basis revenue?

choices.explanation: Correct. Collections plus the AR increase.
Add the increase.
Adjust for the AR change.
Not the computation.

mcqs.explanation: Converting to accrual, revenue equals cash collected plus the increase in receivables.

mcqs.stem: $200,000 was paid for expenses. Prepaid expenses rose $5,000 and accrued liabilities rose $8,000. What is accrual-basis expense?

choices.explanation: Higher prepaids reduce expense.
Correct. 200 − 5 + 8.
Not the computation.
Higher accruals add expense.

mcqs.explanation: Accrual expense equals cash paid, less the prepaid increase, plus the accrued liability increase.

mcqs.stem: Which adjustment is typical of the modified cash basis?

choices.explanation: That's accrual.
That's pure cash basis.
Correct. Modifications with substantial support.
That is not typical.

mcqs.explanation: The modified cash basis adds items with substantial support, such as depreciation of capital assets.

mcqs.stem: How are assets presented in personal financial statements?

choices.explanation: That is not used for PFS.
That is not used for PFS.

choices.text: At the lower of cost or market
choices.explanation: That is not used for PFS.
Correct. PFS use current values.

mcqs.explanation: Personal financial statements present assets at estimated current values and liabilities at current amounts.

mcqs.stem: In personal financial statements, how are taxes on unrealized appreciation presented?

choices.explanation: Correct. Shown between liabilities and net worth.
They're presented.
They're shown separately.
Not the treatment.

mcqs.explanation: PFS show estimated income taxes on differences between current values and tax bases.

mcqs.stem: When must an entity use the liquidation basis of accounting?

choices.text: Whenever going concern is in doubt
choices.explanation: Doubt alone isn't enough.
Correct. It applies when liquidation is imminent.
Not the trigger.
It is not optional.

mcqs.explanation: The liquidation basis applies when liquidation is imminent, unless under a plan from inception.

mcqs.stem: A cash-basis entity receives a $10,000 customer deposit for work next year. How is it reported?

choices.explanation: That's accrual.
That's accrual.
Correct. The cash basis records receipts.
Cash basis records it now.

mcqs.explanation: Under the pure cash basis, revenue is recognized when cash is received.

mcqs.stem: An individual owns 100% of a business. How is it presented in personal financial statements?

choices.explanation: That is not done in PFS.
Use current value.
It is a personal asset.
Correct. A closely held business is presented as a single net amount.

mcqs.explanation: A business interest in PFS is shown as a single investment at estimated current value.

mcqs.stem: A company reports on the **modified cash basis**. Which modification is generally acceptable?

choices.text: Accruing revenue and receivables for all credit sales
choices.explanation: That is a full accrual adjustment; it turns the statements into GAAP rather than a modified cash basis.

choices.text: Capitalizing purchased equipment and recording depreciation
choices.explanation: Correct. This is a common modification with substantial support.
Upward revaluation of land is not generally accepted.
Special purpose framework statements still need adequate disclosure.

mcqs.explanation: Modifications to the cash basis must have substantial support — for example, capitalizing and depreciating long-lived assets or accruing income taxes. Modifications that amount to full accrual accounting are not appropriate.

flashcards.back: Cash · Modified cash · Income tax · Regulatory · Contractual · Other (e.g., FRF for SMEs).
Statement of **assets and liabilities arising from cash transactions**; statement of **revenues collected and expenses paid**.
Cash collected + ending AR − beginning AR (+ write-offs if using gross AR) + beginning unearned − ending unearned.
Cash paid + ending accrued liability − beginning accrued liability + beginning prepaid − ending prepaid.

flashcards.front: Bad debts under the income tax basis
Required disclosure for special purpose frameworks
flashcards.back: Describe the basis and how it **differs from GAAP** (effects need not be quantified), plus GAAP-like informative disclosures.
Capitalize & depreciate fixed assets, record long-term debt, accrue income taxes.
